notes: The s1 floor-plan view adds a footprint trail from the stand to the closing door. That builds a visible walkout without depicting a person, which fits the no-person source limit.

s3 menu-tap is framed as a medium shot with a seated guest while the phone and tapping hands are built as separate arms. Whether limbs and body read as one person, and at matching scale, is a phone-scope risk. It is flagged here, not decided from code.
In s9 viewfinder-hunt the hand-off release is built as handOff [140*release, 1300*release]. The withdrawal path of the hand is a phone and native question.

The performed turn (s8 folder slides in, opens and keeps the box blank) and the closing tags are implemented on the same jar and printer rig as earlier scenes. The source limits are implemented as tags and disclosures, with no person named.
Code approval covers only the funded capture. It grants no pixel, motion or film approval.

story_review.one_viewing_summary: Planned chain from above: footprints leave the empty station and the phone rings. The panel Haniya lights in place of a job ad. A guest scans, taps and pays, and the paid mark is followed into the printer, which prints as the wok flares. The ledger takes the owner's figure and an owner count stamp. Coins cross the pass into the jar under FOX 26. The rule card lights the cook line, the folder's box stays blank, a customer hesitates at the code, and the close tags the jar beside the printed ticket.
story_review.opening_to_ending: The opening question is answered on the same printer and jar rig the film built. The closing image is planned to hold ticket, jar and both tags together.
story_review.weakest_transition: s3 code-scan overhead to menu-tap medium (19.05 s). The cut changes scale and introduces a seated guest whose relationship to the tapping hand is unproven in code.

strongest_frame: s4 pass-wide into the paid-line plan push-in and ticket-print (23.9 to 27.1 s). The camera follows the paid token to the printer, and the lamp, ticket and flare are clock-driven state on the same rig. In s6 (35.2 to 39.2 s) the pass-overhead view links the coins back to the printer and ticket, so the money and the order share one place.
weakest_frame: s10 stand-wide (53.81 to 56.72 s). The order card and slip arc on the panel are planned in a wide framing for 2.91 s with no guest interaction, so 'software now takes the order' is carried at small scale. Its legibility is a phone-scope question.
